children: Raw sugar futures on ICE steadied on Friday as investors refrained from betting on higher prices given forecasts for improved weather conditions in top grower Brazil.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
​settled down 0.08 cent, or 0.5%, at 17.50 cents per lb, having closed down 1% on Thursday.
* Sugar has been drifting higher of late as excess rains in Brazil have disrupted harvesting, but investors are growing reticent to bet on further gains at these price levels.

* "The market appears to be drifting now after a rush to 19.00 cents on the open yesterday. It now appears the remainder of the month will be dry (in Brazil)," said independent broker and consultant Michael McDougall.
* Broker ADMIS, meanwhile, pointed to reports there were enough rains in Thailand and the southern Philippines this month to improve the moisture profile in areas that were previously too dry.
* White sugar
fell 1.4% to $502.60 a metric ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled up 3.25 cents, or 1.2%, at $2.786 per lb​​, but still posted a weekly fall of 5.4%.
* Arabica remains under pressure overall from expectations that Brazil harvested a record crop in 2026/27, and from signs crop flows from Brazil to consuming regions are picking up.
* In addition, Brazil's 2027/28 is off to a good start as "ample rains have induced flowering, and the growing areas appear to be getting good follow-up rains," said ADMIS.
* The good physical demand was also noted as somewhat supportive.
* "If this continues (high Brazil exports), my flat price pessimism might change with it. Or diffs will skyrocket closer to year end and off-season Jan-Jun," said Cazarini Trading Company in a note.
* Robusta coffee
rose 2.3% to $3,367 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​​settled up £22, or 0.5%, at £4,205 per ton. The market posted a 7% weekly gain.
* No. 2 cocoa grower Ghana will open its 2026/27 cocoa season on Friday and announce the farmgate price for the season, five sources told Reuters.

* "Evidence of a broad recovery in cocoa supply is strengthening the case for a substantial surplus, but delayed West African crop movement, weather threats and financing constraints mean the market remains vulnerable to sharp rallies," said industry newsletter CocoaRadar.com.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.5% to $5,619 a ton.
